objective.statement: A local-first tool that routes developer queries to the most capable available LLM based on task complexity, minimising latency and cost.
objective.for: Developers running local and cloud LLM backends simultaneously.
objective.problem: Developers must manually decide which LLM to use per task, switching tools and accepting unnecessary latency or cost for simple queries.

functionalRequirements.description: Developer can submit a query and receive a response routed to an appropriate backend.
functionalRequirements.notes: Routing decision is invisible to the developer unless they opt into verbose mode.

functionalRequirements.description: Developer can configure which backends are available and their priority order.
Developer can view a log of past queries, which backend handled each, and response latency.
Developer can force a specific backend for a query by passing an explicit override flag.
Gateway falls back to the next available backend if the preferred backend is unavailable.

nonFunctionalRequirements.scale: Routing overhead in milliseconds added to a query round-trip
nonFunctionalRequirements.meter: Measured locally with a no-op backend at 50 sequential queries

nonFunctionalRequirements.scale: Percentage of queries that fail due to gateway error (not backend error)
nonFunctionalRequirements.meter: Error rate measured over 1000 consecutive queries in integration test

nonFunctionalRequirements.scale: Supported operating systems without code changes
nonFunctionalRequirements.meter: Manual smoke test on each platform after each release

userStories.capability: submit a query without specifying a backend
userStories.outcome: I can focus on my task instead of managing which model to use

userStories.capability: configure backend priority from a config file
userStories.outcome: I can adjust routing behaviour without modifying code

userStories.capability: inspect which backend handled each of my past queries
userStories.outcome: I can understand routing decisions and tune my configuration

userStories.capability: force a specific backend for a single query
userStories.outcome: I can test a backend directly without changing my configuration

successCriteria.description: A query submitted without a backend override is routed and returns a response with no manual backend selection required.
successCriteria.verificationMethod: Automated integration test with two configured backends.

successCriteria.description: When the preferred backend is down, the gateway routes to the next configured backend and the query succeeds.
successCriteria.verificationMethod: Integration test with primary backend disabled.

successCriteria.description: Routing overhead does not exceed 50ms on the reference machine at 50 sequential queries.
All REQ-001 through REQ-005 pass their acceptance tests.

nonGoals.reason: Deferred to a future version; single-developer use only for this release.
Out of scope; CLI and config file are sufficient for the target user.
Out of scope; gateway routes to existing backends, does not modify them.

nonGoals.capability: Billing and cost tracking across cloud providers
nonGoals.reason: Deferred; cost visibility is a logging concern handled in a later version.
